claims.content: To display a list of up to 10 recorded player statistics, including the player's name, number of block movements, and time used to solve the headache.

goal.raw_text: To display a list of up to 10 recorded player statistics, including the player's name, number of block movements, and time used to solve the headache.

claims.content: Player
The statistic file must exist and be accessible for reading player statistics.
The game must have recorded at least one set of player statistics (name, block movement number, time passed) in the statistic file.
End of the game (see chapter 3.2.2.1) or menu selection.

trigger.raw_text: End of the game (see chapter 3.2.2.1) or menu selection.

claims.content: The system reads the player statistics from the statistic file of the game.
The system displays the Player Statistics Window, which is composed of a listbox of 10 lines.
Each line in the listbox displays the name of a player, the number of block movements, and the time used by the player to solve the headache.
If the statistic file cannot be correctly updated (e.g., due to wrong permissions or disk full) during processing, an error message is displayed.
If the file was correctly updated, there is no output.
If not, like wrong permissions or disk full, an error message is displayed.
The Player Statistics Window is displayed to the user.
A listbox of 10 lines, each composed of a player's name, block movement number, and time used to solve the headache, is visible in the window.
